Input consists of N>=3, explicit rational a_i>0 and b_i, rational time T, and integer p>=1. Let B be the total binary input length excluding T and p. **At the mathematical existence level, yes:** for explicitly supplied rational positive periodic Toda initial data and rational target time, the repaired lemmas supply a polynomial-bit algorithm with original-state max error epsilon, including exact closed gaps. ## Precise root-isolation import, checked

Mehlhorn–Sagraloff–Wang, *From Approximate Factorization to Root Isolation with Application to Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition*, [arXiv:1301.4870v2, Theorem 5](https://arxiv.org/html/1301.4870), states that an integer polynomial of degree n and coefficient bits tau has all distinct roots and their multiplicities isolated in soft-O(n^3+n^2 tau) bit operations; refinement to disk radius below 2^-kappa costs soft-O(n^3+n^2 tau+n kappa). Its proof computes the distinct-root count from p/gcd(p,p'), and normalizes by the exact leading coefficient. Thus there is no distinct-root-count or leading-coefficient promise in our rational-polynomial application. Clear denominators first. I inspected the theorem and proof, not just its abstract.
